source.objectiveEnglish: Say what is missing, what has not arrived yet, and when you need more, less or another.
source.focusSpanish: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro on the jobsite
source.speakingEnglish: Tell a coworker what is missing, what has not arrived yet, and what the crew needs more or less of today.

archivedDraft.title: Confirm tomorrow's meeting
archivedDraft.scene: Tanaka asks site supervisor Sato about tomorrow morning's crew meeting; Tanaka mishears the correct time and Sato corrects it
materialDrift: Old Japanese Foundation 8 asks about tomorrow's meeting time and place with Tanaka and Sato; current source is Luis and Ana's missing delivery, ladder, water mix, open trench and safety-glasses workday.

cards.sourceNoteInternal: Use otra with feminine nouns, and never un otro: otra escalera.

cards.sourceSpanish: No hay nadie en el andamio.
cards.sourceNoteInternal: Spanish keeps both negatives: no hay nadie.
cards.japaneseDraft: 足場には誰もいません。

cards.sourceSpanish: Nunca trabajamos sin lentes de seguridad.
cards.sourceEnglish: We never work without safety glasses.
cards.japaneseDraft: 保護メガネなしでは決して作業しません。
納品はまだ届いていません。
別のはしごが必要です。
不足しているものは何もありません。

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis, el capataz, revisa la obra con Ana a las 7.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis, the foreman, checks the jobsite with Ana at 7.
reader.japaneseDraft: 現場監督のルイスは7時にアナと現場を確認します。

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: La entrega todavía no llega.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: The delivery hasn't arrived yet.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「納品はまだ届いていません。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Sin bloques, nadie trabaja en la pared hoy.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: Without blocks, nobody works on the wall today.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「ブロックがなければ、今日は誰も壁の作業をしません。」
アナ：「別のはしごが必要です。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana: La mezcla necesita menos agua.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana: The mix needs less water.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: La zanja abierta es un peligro para la cuadrilla.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: The open trench is a hazard for the crew.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「開いたままの掘削溝は作業班にとって危険です。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Ponemos más cinta de precaución alrededor de la zanja.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: We put more caution tape around the trench.

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana: Nunca trabajamos sin lentes de seguridad.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana: We never work without safety glasses.
reader.japaneseDraft: アナ：「保護メガネなしで作業することは決してありません。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Hay lentes para todos en la caja y no falta nada.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: There are glasses for everyone in the box, and nothing is missing.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「箱には全員分の保護メガネがあり、足りないものはありません。」

decisionsNeeded: Resolve isolated never, nobody, nothing, less and caution-tape Japanese senses before selecting cards 1–3, 6 and 10; source Spanish no/nunca/nadie/nada grammar does not transfer word for word.
Resolve 'mix needs less water' without suggesting an unverified mix ratio or procedure; leave card 15 and Reader 5 Japanese unset pending qualified construction/source review.

Confirm open trench and caution tape terminology and scope with qualified Japanese and construction reviewers. Reader 7 is unset, and Reader 6 is conditional; do not convert a scene claim into worksite instructions.
Preserve Luis, Ana, 7 o'clock, undelivered blocks, wall, another ladder, open trench, safety glasses and box in source order; archived tomorrow-meeting scene is a separate lesson.
Map Spanish negative patterns to natural Japanese negation and distinguish not yet from never as a curriculum choice; author exact six modes, forms, speaking, dictionary and saved-item semantics.
Verify qualified exact text before audio synthesis and make separate technical and listening decisions for every clip.
